crowdsourced_ai_results.analysis: The sample is a standard Windows command-line FTP (File Transfer Protocol) client, likely the legitimate Microsoft ftp.exe. The decompiled code reveals standard FTP client functionality, including command parsing for RETR (download), STOR (upload), LIST (directory listing), and USER/PASS (authentication). It uses Winsock for network communication (socket, bind, connect, listen) and supports both active and extended passive modes. Notable features include argument parsing for scripting (-s) and verbosity (-v), as well as a shell escape function (_shell) that executes local commands via the COMSPEC environment variable. No indicators of malicious intent, such as obfuscation, unauthorized persistence, or hidden C2 communication, were observed.
